issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
text:
On XX/XX/2020 I applied for a home loan with Rocket Mortgage and I was denied because of something called a " Mortgage Credit Score. '' I have never heard of such a thing and I was a Realtor for many years. And I have purchased 4 homes myself, so I'm pretty versed in the loan process. 

I would have never filled out the credit application if they had explained that my credit score ( which was good enough for an FHA Loan according to FHA.GOV ) was meaningless. 

I have painstakingly worked to improve my credit over the last 2.5 years after leaving my ex who ran my credit into the ground. I haven't attempted to run my credit at all until yesterday. I'm still working hard on my credit and I even pay to have it monitored and reported via XXXX XXXX. 

Rocket Mortgage 's application is clearly misleading the applicant. They ask for the applicant to choose a credit score range that best represents their credit score, but they never mention a " Mortgage Credit Score '' which will matter most, not their actual credit score. 

Before filling out the application, I called Rocket Mortgage to make sure they would finance tiny houses with FHA loans. The representative said yes and to apply on their site. So I did. 

I had done my homework by checking with FHA for their minimum credit score and they listed a minimum of 580, never mentioning this " Mortgage Credit Score ''. According to XXXX XXXX, I am in the 600 's. So I was immediately denied. I would not have an issue with them denying me if they had CLEARLY stated in the application that everything is not based on your regular credit score, but a " Mortgage Credit Score ''. This is VERY misleading and they don't even offer you a way to leave a review for them online so I can't alert others to be aware of this. 

This hit to my credit report will now bring my score down. Which may not be anything to them, but it's everything to the consumer.

To whom it may concern I am writing to dispute the accuracy of the information on my credit report. Specifically, I am concerned about the false verification of information that is negatively affecting my credit score. 

According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Section 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), consumers have the right to dispute any inaccurate or incomplete information on their credit report with credit bureaus. Furthermore, Section 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ) requires credit bureaus to conduct a reasonable investigation into any disputed information and provide the consumer with a written report of the investigation 's results. 

In my case, I have disputed the accuracy of certain information on my credit report, and the credit bureau has verified it as accurate without conducting a reasonable investigation. This is a clear violation of FCRA Section 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ), which states that credit bureaus must investigate all disputes, including those deemed frivolous. 

Additionally, the credit bureau 's failure to investigate my dispute violates FCRA Section 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ), which requires credit bureaus to modify or delete any inaccurate or incomplete information within 30 days of receiving a dispute from a consumer. 

Therefore, I request that the false verified information be deleted from my credit report immediately in accordance with FCRA Section 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) and that the credit bureau conducts a reasonable investigation into my dispute in compliance with FCRA Section 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ).

issue: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
text: XX/XX/19 purchased a washer and dryer from Best Buy using a " promotional period of 18 months ''. They did not explain that the payments I would be making would not be directed toward the promotional balance until after I noticed that none of my payments were being directed to that balance. Apparently, because they raised my limit in order to purchase these items, they made my minimum payment over {$1000.00} and until that payment was reduced none of the payments were credited to the promotional balance. The purchased items totaled almost {$1700.00}. Since the purchase date, XX/XX/2019, I have made {$1300.00} in payments with none of these payments directed toward the promotional balance. I feel these promotional advertisements are VERY misleading. They lure you in with the promise of no interest for 18 months on a purchase without informing you at the time of purchase how that " promotion '' actually works. I have noticed several complaints concerning the same issue over the past few months. I wish I had been diligent enough to do my homework concerning this " advertisement '' before I made the purchase. However, I believe this is an unfair practice on their part by not informing the consumer before the purchase is made how the " promotional balance '' is paid ( or not paid ).

A loan was taken out with Bank of America in XXXX for a conventional loan. The loan was financed with 5 % down which incurred a monthly private mortgage insurance ( PMI ) fee. This loan was subsequently sold to XXXX XXXX making XXXX XXXX the loan holder. In XXXX, as the property value had increased, and the loan was paid down, an appraisal was made by a lender approved appraisal company, XXXX XXXX, indicating that the current loan to value ratio was at 79 %. Since XXXX XXXX indicates that they would remove PMI when the LTV is less than 80 % the PMI at that point should have been removed. Bank of America which no longer owns the loans should not be allowed to charge a PMI when XXXX XXXX does not charge it. The Homeowner Protection Act indicates that the law was intended to protect against Excessive PMI coverage that provides little extra protection for a lender and does not benefit the borrower. By setting an arbitrary requirement below what the loan holder, XXXX XXXX, is requesting, Bank of America is violating the spirit of the law. Anything in excess of this requirement would be considered Unearned Premium. Bank of America is insuring a product that they do not own, and this is costing the borrower thousands of dollars with no benefit. 

Bank of America also states that a request to remove the PMI can be made when LTV is under 80 %. This becomes a moot statement if the request can be denied even when the assessed LTV is under 80 %. Bank of America should not be allowed to set limits below LTV limits below what is required by law.
